meta.hypothesis: The residual 23% cascade-ion deficit at 10 keV is driven by σ_exc inflation (PHYSICS_DIAGNOSIS §2); lowering SIGMA_EXC_SCALE from 0.5 toward Born (~0.39) should recover the cascade count toward Geant4 509.
meta.method: Flipped SIGMA_EXC_SCALE 0.5->0.39 in helpers.wgsl, regenerated all 8 ESTAR dumps (WebGPU physics, chem off), recounted H3O+ cascade ions + read CSDA and G(H)_init from the harness log. RECOMB_BOOST held at 1.0 (production).
meta.passBar: cascade ratio increases materially toward 1.0 (hypothesis confirmed) OR stays flat (hypothesis REFUTED).

summary.headline: REFUTED: lowering σ_exc 22% (0.5->0.39) moved the 10 keV cascade ratio only 0.766->0.770x (+2 ions/pri). σ_exc is NOT the lever for the residual 23% deficit — at 10 keV excitation is a minority energy-loss channel (ionization dominates), so it is saturated by 0.5. The deficit has a different, still-unidentified cause (not σ_exc; σ_ion is the wrong direction per E6b).

conclusion: Corrects PHYSICS_DIAGNOSIS §2: the residual cascade deficit at 10 keV is NOT a σ_exc-vs-G(H) tradeoff. σ_exc matters at sub-keV (CSDA, E5d) but is saturated for the 10 keV cascade. Production keeps σ_exc=0.5 (0.39 gave no meaningful gain). The cause of the 23% is reopened.
